Khuddakanikāya
or Khuddaka Gantha. fifth division of Sutta Piṭaka; according to one [Page185-b] view Khuddakaº includes Vinaya an. Abhidhamma with 15 books, beg. with Khuddakapāṭha; acc. to Dīghabhāṇaka school, it contains 12 books, an. acc. to Majjhimabhāṇaka, 15 books.
See JPTS. 1888, p. 27.
For a study of the original form of Pāli Khuddaka Nikāya an. its development an. chronology of individual sections, see E. Mayeda, J. of Ind. an. Bud. Studies, Tokyo, 498-504 (from rear).
Cabaton II. 91 (sections 1-6, from Khu. pāṭha to Itivuttaka). 123 (sections 5-7 an. 14). Colombo p. 48. Colombo D. I. 1696-97. 1699 (Udāna). 1767. Fausboll 67-70 (sections). IO. Pāli p. 60 (nos. 16-17). Kandy II. p. 1 (in 15 sections). Oxf. Pāli p. 30 (Dhammapada).
Pt.. (1) See Suttapiṭaka, The Royal Siamese edn., Bangkok, 1894. (2) For PTS. edns. in Roman script. see under the different sections, Khu. pāṭha etc. (3) Nālandā Devanāgarī Pāli Ser. 1959, in 7 Vol..
Eng. transl.. (1) Mrs. Rhys Davids. PTS. transl. Ser. 23. 1931 ff. (2) along with Dhammapada an. Suttapiṭaka, by Narada Thera. London, 1954.
--C. Aṭṭhakathā. Colombo p. 50.

Khuddakapāṭha
Bud. Pāli. first section of Khuddakanikāya; comprises nine short texts. Br. Mus. Pāli p. 139. Cabaton II. 92 (I). Cambr. Uni. Pāli p. 145. Colombo p. 48 (2 mss.). Colombo D. I. 74. IO. Pāli p. 60 (no. 16a). Kandy II. p. 1. Paris Pāli p. 33 (2 mss.).
Pt.. (1) in Roman script. edn. with Eng. transl. an. notes by R. C. Childers. JRAS. NS. IV. 1870, p.. 309-39; same reprinted, Buddhist Review, I. iv. 1909, p.. 266-74. with [Page186-a. Sinhalese transl. Colombo, 1889. (2) in Siamese script. Royal Siamese Ed.. of Tripiṭaka Vol. 25, Bangkok, 1894. (3) with Eng. transl., S. Kumar. Calcutta, 1909. (4) with transl., P. M. Tin. Rangoon, 1913. (5) with C. Paramatthajotikā, in Roman script. edn. by Helmer Smith from a collation by Mabel Hunt, PTS. 77, 1915. (6) with C. Paramatthajotikā, in Sinhalese characters, edited by Acharya Welipitiye Dewananda Thera an. revised by Mahagoda Siri Ñanissara Thera, Simon Hewavitarne Bequest, 11, Colombo, 1922. (7) Ed.. an. transl. by Mrs. Rhys Davids, Minor Anthologies of the Pāli Canon. Part I. Sacred Books of the Buddhists Ser. 7. (PTS. transl. Ser. 23), 1931. (8) with Eng. transl., N. K. Bhagawat, 1931.
Eng. transl., ‘Some sayings of the Buddha’, p.. 53 ff.; ‘Minor Readings an. Illustrations’, Bhikku Ñānanoli, PTS. 1961.
German transl. by Karl Seidenstu7cker, Breslau, Walter Markgraf, 1910.
See also ‘What is Khuddaka Pāṭha’ by P. K. Das, Mahābodhi 33 (1925) p.. 72-5.
--C. Aṭṭhakathā, Paramatthajotikā, by Buddhaghoṣa. Br. Mus. Pāli p. 140 (inc.). Cabaton II. 92 (II). Colombo D. I. 93.
Pt.. See above under text.
--Khuddakapāṭhapakaraṇa from. Fausboll 67-68.
--Tirokudda Sutta (7th text) from. Colombo D. I. 373. 374 (wants beg.).

Khuddasikkhā
Bud. Pāli. a compendium of Vinaya, mostly in verses, according to [Page186-b] its last stanzas composed by Dhammasiri of Ceylon; according to some Burmese histories, by a. associate of Dharmasiri, viz. Mahāsāmi of Ceylon; dated variously in 440 A. D., 6th or 7th Cent. (Mu7ller), C. 11th Cent. (Geiger).
See Gandhavaṁsa, JPTS. 1886, p.. 61-70 (JPTS. 1888, p. 27); JPTS. 1883, p.. 86-87; Wint. HIL. II. p. 221 an. Geiger, Pāli Lit. an. Lang. (Eng. transl., Cal. Uni. 1943), p.. 35, 39.
Br. Mus. Pāli II. p. 110 (2 mss.; one fr.). Cabaton II. 371. 671 (I). Colombo p. 50.; Colombo D. I. 38, 39. Copen. Pāli p. 147. Fausboll 23. 24. 148. IO. Pāli p.. 68 (no. 3). 123 (no. 105, 2 mss.; one with explanation). (no. 106). Paris Pāli p. 34.
Pt.. (1) Ed. by D.. Edward Mu7ller, JPTS. 1883, p.. 86-121 (with comparative table of Khuddasikkhā passages an. Oldenberg's Vinaya, ibid. p.. 131-2). (2) with Sinhalese paraphrase. Colombo, 1894. (3) in a collection of four Pāli works on Vinaya. work no. 3. Rangoon, 1898. (4) in Sinhalese characters, with C. Sumaṅgalapasādani of Saṅgharakkhita. Colombo, 1898. (5) with Burmese interpretation, Kyaiklat, 1912. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1892-1906. 150. 855. 1906-28. 266.
--C. Ṭīkā in Pāli. Cabaton II. 672 (I). Colombo p. 51.
--C. Dīpanī. Cabaton II. p.. 167 (81-82) (with French transl.). 371-3. Paris Pāli p. 34 (2 mss.).
--C. Porāṇa-ṭīkā by Revata or Mahāyasa, end of 11th Cent. A. D. [Page187-a.
See JPTS. 1908, p. 97 fn.; Malalasekhara, Pāli Lit. of Ceylon, p.. 77-8; Bode, Pāli Lit. of Burma, p. 24 fn. 1; Geiger, Pāli Lit. an. Lang. (Eng. transl., Cal. Uni. 1943). p. 39.
--C. Ṭīkā Sumaṅgalapasādani by Saṅgharakkhita Thera; pupil of Sārīputta an. Medhaṅkara of Udumbaragiri (latter part of 12th Cent. A. D.). Cambr. Uni. Pāli p. 146. Colombo D. I. 40.

Khuddasvāmin
Inscriptional poet. Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum IV. p. 171.

Khuddī_Jhā
elder brother of Apūcha Jhā (a. of Makarandakaraṇa, 19th Cent. A. D. Mithilā III. 245).
See NCC. I. Revised edn. p.. 255b256a.

Khuddī_Jhā
son of Umādatta Maithila of Benares.
--Nāgeśoktiprakāśa. notes on Laghuśabdenduśekhara.
Pt.. Benares, 1899. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1892-1906. 310.
--C. Naukā on Vyutpattivāda.
Pt.. Madhubani (Darbhanga D..), 1910. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1906-28. 298. 496 an. IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1938. p. 1349.
